speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. I notice you have some skin lesions you would like me to evaluate for potential oncologic issues. To begin, can you tell me how long these lesions have been present and if they are changing in size, shape, or color?

speaker: Patient
text: 62-year-old male. The patient has recently immigrated to the US from Africa and seeks evaluation for a non-healing, red, crusty lesion on the shaft of his penis and a similar lesion on his left middle finger. Previous treatments in his home country for syphilis and eczema have been unsuccessful. The patient is a smoker, with a history of two packs per day for the last 30 years.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Squamous Cell Carcinoma.

The patient's history of heavy smoking, African origin (a risk factor for HPV-associated penile cancer), and presentation of non-healing, crusty lesions on both the penis and an extremity strongly suggest a diagnosis of Squamous Cell Carcinoma. I will proceed with requesting a biopsy and imaging to confirm the stage and extent of the disease.

REQUEST TEST: Biopsy_of_penile_lesion and Biopsy_of_finger_lesion
REQUEST IMAGES: Dermoscopy_of_penile_lesion and Clinical_photos_of_lesions
